spec: SPEC 2.1 (appending missing lines) and 9.3 (resolving a conflict)
about: `required` lists the required lines of each file, in order. `append` cases: the text of the file when a group is opened, and the text after appending the missing required lines (an empty `text` is a missing file). `merge` cases: the two versions in conflict and the result; where `symmetric` is true the result must be the same with the two versions swapped. Text is given with explicit \n and \r\n.

append.name: the .gitignore plugin 0.1.0 wrote gets the other two lines
a file without a final newline gets one before the appended lines
a missing file becomes the required lines
a file that has every line is returned unchanged, whatever else it holds (CRLF, no final newline)
existing CRLF lines are left alone; the appended lines use LF
other lines are never reordered or removed

merge.name: the other lines of both sides, sorted, then the required lines
nothing else in the file can come after, and so override, a required line
two groups joined: each side's file is kept
CRLF line ends and blank lines do not matter
identical sides give that file plus the required lines
two empty files give just the required lines
a required line found among the other lines moves to its place at the end
sorting is by UTF-8 bytes, not by UTF-16 code units (U+FF5E sorts before U+1F600 in UTF-8, after it in UTF-16)
